gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in named independent tests, two of its four picks lasted only about a month on battery alone and so depend on the solar panel: Techtest.org measured about one month for the Tapo C660 against TP-Link's 120-day claim and about one month for the Reolink Argus 4 Pro; Basic Tutorials also got just under a month for the Argus 4 Pro. Meanwhile SafeWise kept the eufy SoloCam S340 at or near 100% for about a month of heavy use on solar.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages and one top result. rottenwifi.com 'Best Solar-Powered Home Security Cameras for 2026' (cited) uses only maker specs and lab claims, with no independent runtime tests. reolink.com's 'Best Reolink Solar Security Camera 2026 Guide' (cited) uses only Reolink specs and Reolink lab claims. homegearlab.org (rank 6) says 'Every sunlight and battery figure on this page is the maker's own' and 'We found no independent data comparing how these panels keep up in winter or shade', and it does not cover the C660 or the Eco Ultra. None of these pages gives a named reviewer's runtime or solar result for any card ChatGPT showed.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's 'best overall' pick, the eufy SoloCam S340, because it is the only card with a named month-long test that held about 100% charge on about 2 h of sun a day. It also weakens the case for the Tapo C660 and Argus 4 Pro wherever the panel gets poor sun or in winter. Both lasted only about a month on battery alone, far short of the C660's 120-day claim, and Techtest.org says the C660 needs several manual recharges in winter. The Argus Eco Ultra card has no independent test at all, only maker claims and mixed owner reviews.
